text:
sara_acme: Hey folks — urgent for our integration. We're seeing streams drop partway through the response (usually ~30-45s), the client reconnects automatically, and the billing console shows duplicate token usage for the same logical request (double-billed). Request id from our logs: req_abc123xyz, region: us-west1. Using redwood-js 1.3.7. Noticed this started after a traffic spike yesterday.

maria_support: sorry you're hitting this — can you confirm whether the client gets a 429 or a connection close? any server error lines? also paste a short repro if you can.

sara_acme: No explicit 500; client reports connection closed then on reconnect sometimes we get a partial continuation, sometimes a brand new stream. I see a 429 event in our client logs during some of the disconnects: "HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests" followed by the SSE connection closing. Billing shows two sessions for req_abc123xyz and req_abc123xyz-reconnect which together equal the length we expected.

maria_support: thanks. Can you run a quick curl repro and paste headers? e.g. something like below helped us earlier: 

```bash
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  -d '{"model":"rw-large","prompt":"x","max_tokens":4000}' \\n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate/stream
```

If you can capture the request_id returned in initial 200 chunk and the final status code that'd help.

sara_acme: sending now. received initial chunk with request_id=req_abc123xyz, then after ~38s got a chunk: `event: rate_limit\ndata: {"code":429,"message":"quota exceeded"}` then connection closed. Client retried immediately (default sdk auto-retry) and opened a fresh stream with new req id req_abc123xyz-r1. Both show token counts in billing.

jonas_platform: internal note — common pattern: our streaming path reserves tokens as they are generated; if a stream is terminated mid-generation and we don't correctly release or reconcile reserved tokens, a reconnect that starts a new stream consumes more tokens resulting in apparent double-billing. We'll need logs from the serving nodes around req_abc123xyz.

maria_support: I've asked the customer to attach full server logs and the SDK stack trace. they uploaded "/var/logs/acme/redwood_stream.log" with timestamps. Placing snippets below.

```
[2026-01-17T12:23:15Z] request=req_abc123xyz reserve_tokens=312 reserved_by=stream-gen node=serve-03
[2026-01-17T12:23:53Z] request=req_abc123xyz event=rate_limit code=429 limiter=minute_token_rate node=serve-03
[2026-01-17T12:23:53Z] request=req_abc123xyz connection=closed reason=client_disconnect
[2026-01-17T12:23:53Z] request=req_abc123xyz release_tokens=ERROR err=connection_reset_unhandled node=serve-03
[2026-01-17T12:23:53Z] request=req_abc123xyz-r1 reserve_tokens=312 node=serve-07
[2026-01-17T12:23:55Z] billing.ledger credit=0 debit=312 request=req_abc123xyz
[2026-01-17T12:23:55Z] billing.ledger debit=312 request=req_abc123xyz-r1
```

keisha_eng: I can repro locally using high token-per-sec prompt pattern + SDK auto-retry. Repro steps: start a long-stream with chunked generation where token rate > limiter threshold (I used a prompt that forces 100 tokens/s on a small sequence length) and then induce a 429 from the rate limiter mid-stream. Because the client auto-retries it opens a fresh connection; our ledger currently charges for reserved tokens on terminate and also charges the new session — the problem is that the reserve->release path failed due to the connection_reset path; release wasn't reconciled before ledger write.

keisha_eng: quick repro curl (internal test):
```bash
# node env: redwood-js 1.3.7 default retry behavior
TOKEN=redwood-test
# attack the limiter by requesting a very bursty generation
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  -d '{"model":"rw-large","prompt":"<burst-token-prompt>","max_tokens":2000,"stream":true}' \\n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate/stream
```
You should see `event: rate_limit` then client reconnect if sdk auto-retry is enabled.

ravi_sre: logs show serve-03 hit limiter and then a release_tokens failed stack trace: 
```
release_tokens failed: context canceled (connection_reset_unhandled)
ledger.commit: debit(req_abc123xyz, 312)
ledger.commit: debit(req_abc123xyz-r1, 312)
```
This explains double-charging. The real bug is twofold: (1) rate-limiter throws 429 mid-stream but doesn't ensure proper token reclamation when connection drops and (2) the SDK auto-retry opens a brand new logical request (new request_id) instead of a resume/append semantics, so billing sees two distinct charges.

keisha_eng: fix plan
- immediate mitigation (within hours): stop SDK auto-retry for streaming on our hosted SDKs (v1.3.8 patch) and add client-side guidance to set `retry: 0` for streams in docs.
- short term (1-2 days): server change to aggressively reconcile reserved tokens on connection termination paths and gate ledger commit until reconciliation completes (small window).
- long term: support resumable stream id so client reconnects can resume the same logical session (no new ledger debit).

emma_billing: we can issue an automated credit for impacted token counts once engineering gives the list of affected request_ids. For this customer we'll credit the amount corresponding to both debits for req_abc123xyz and req_abc123xyz-r1.

maria_support: status update — keisha pushed a mitigation to disable streaming auto-retry in hosted SDKs (redwood-js v1.3.8) and a server hotfix to reconcile reserved tokens on close for in-flight 429s. Patch IDs: serve-runtime v2.7.14-reconcile. Deploy bot below.

deploy-bot: deploy started: serve-runtime v2.7.14-reconcile -> us-west1 (canary)
deploy-bot: canary passed on serve-04 after 2m
deploy-bot: rollout 40% complete -> us-west1

keisha_eng: rolled a fix that waits up to 250ms for release_tokens reconciler to complete before ledger.commit on connection error — this prevents the double-commit race. Also added extra logging for `reconcile_id` and `orig_request_id` for future triage.

ravi_sre: monitoring created to alert when a single logical session results in >1 ledger debit within 10s. threshold: 2 debits. rule id: SRE-STREAM-DOUBLEBILL.

maria_support: Emma/billing — please proceed with credit for acme account for the two debits. Keisha — can you attach the list of request_ids flagged by the reconciler for this customer?

keisha_eng: uploaded list to ticket: [req_abc123xyz, req_abc123xyz-r1, req_abc199999, req_abc199999-r1]. Filter done via `reconcile_id` map.

emma_billing: credited 624 tokens (equiv) to acme-prod account and applied a 30-day monitoring credit to avoid noise while they validate. Also opened a billing followup to review ledger idempotency for streaming (BILL-STREAM-23).

sara_acme: applied the SDK v1.3.8 change (disabled stream auto-retry) and verified in staging — streams either fail and we surface the 429 to the client so we can backoff, or complete normally. After your deploy we hit a previously failing flow and the ledger now shows a single debit. Confirmed with the customer: they ran 10 repro attempts and all now show single-charge behavior.

maria_support: closing loop — root cause: race between rate-limiter 429 + connection reset path where reserved tokens were not reconciled before ledger commit + client SDK auto-retry opening new request ids. Remediation: server reconcile hotfix (v2.7.14-reconcile), SDK guidance and patch (redwood-js v1.3.8), monitoring rule SRE-STREAM-DOUBLEBILL, and billing credits applied.

sara_acme: thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll keep an eye on volume and upgrade SDK across our fleet.

keisha_eng: follow ups: implement resumable stream id (longer-term), add more robust idempotency guards in ledger, and publish a short KB about recommended streaming retry behavior and diagnostic sniffers (how to capture request_id + reconcile_id).

maria_support: marking resolved for this thread. If anything else pops up please reopen with logs and request_ids. :thumbsup:
